Meeting Schedule

The regular meetings of the City Council are held on the second and fourth Tuesday of each month,

  1
 closed session business will usually commence at 5:30 p.m., when scheduled, and general business
session will commence at 6:30 p.m.

Brown Act

Agendas are drafted to accurately state what the legislative body is being asked to consider. The
legislative body can take action on "all items" listed on the agenda and be in compliance with the open
meeting laws. Under the Brown Act, no action may be taken on a matter unless it is listed on the
agenda, or unless certain emergency or special circumstances exist. The governing body may direct
staff to investigate and/or schedule certain matters for consideration at a future meeting.

City's Vision Statement

We envision a thriving, safe and inclusive community where everyone has the opportunity to access
exceptional services, education and support to be resilient and live full, vibrant lives.

Public Communications

Public Comments on agenda items are limited to three (3) minutes. All comments are to be addressed
directly to the Agency Members not to the members of the public.

Emails for public comment received prior to 12pm on the day of the Council Meeting will be summarized
by the City Clerk, not read in its entirety. A copy of the email will be provided to the City Council and will
also be available at the City Clerk's Office for public review. A copy of each email will be recorded for
public record and noted on the official minutes of tonight's meeting.

Comments From The Audience - Non-Agenda Items
During this time, members of the public may address the City Council regarding any items not
listed on the agenda and within the subject matter jurisdiction of the City Council and not on
this agenda. Comments from the audience will be limited to three (3) minutes per speaker;
unless authorized by the Mayor, the time limit may not be extended by utilizing another
member's time. There will be no debate or action on items not listed on the agenda unless
authorized by law. The collective initial period of time for comments from the audience shall
be limited to 45 minutes. Any speaker that did not get a chance to speak during this segment
due to the 45-minute limitations will be able to speak at the end of the meeting prior to
adjournment.

Note: The City Council desires to provide all members of the public with the opportunity to
address the Council. Nevertheless, obscene language, comments intended to
disrupt/interfere, other actions which disrupt the progress of the meeting or slanderous
comments will not be tolerated and may result in ejection and/or may constitute a violation of

 GENERAL NOTICE TO THE PUBLIC

The City Council adopted new rules relating to the conduct of the public meetings, proceedings, and
business in the City of South Gate on July 12, 2022, (Resolution 2022-38-CC) and go into effect on
August 1, 2022. Resolution #2022-38-CC is available at the City Clerk’s Office.

MEETING SCHEDULE

Regular meetings of the City Council are held on the second and fourth Tuesday of each month, closed
session meetings will commence at 5:30 p.m. unless posted otherwise on its agenda. The regular City
Council meetings will commence at 6:30 p.m. Agendas are available at the following locations: City Clerk
Office, Public Notice Boards at City Hall, and on the City’s web page at https://www.cityofsouthgate.org

The Public can sign up to receive automatic notices of postings of agendas for the City Council or any
other Commission or Board of the City of South Gate. Visit the City webpage and click on the Agenda &
Minutes icon. That will take you the page where an individual can enter their email in the “Email
Updates” box to register.

PUBLIC COMMENT/PARTICIPATION

Any person may request to address a legislative body during a public meeting. The Presiding Officer will
call upon those present in the Council Chambers first. After all speakers in the Chambers have spoken,
the Presiding Officer will call upon those participating via zoom or teleconference.

Speakers are limited to three (3) minutes on any item listed on the agenda, including public hearings.
Under Comments from the Audience portion, speakers are also limited to a single three (3) minutes time
limit. Comments from the Audience is initially limited to 45 minutes at each meeting. Any speaker still
wishing to speak, that did not speak, will have an addition Comments from the Audience opportunity after
the last business item is finished. The Presiding Officer may extend the time limit as long as there is no
objection from the City Council as a body.

To ensure that the public is able to participate, the City provides the opportunity to submit their
comments in person, virtually, email, phone call, mail and any other method which may become
available. Methods of participation may be subject to change during other such times when a State of
Emergency, Health Order or State Executive Order limits in-person participation.

CURFEW

In absence of a motion duly adopted by majority vote of the City Council, the Presiding Officer may
adjourn the City Council meetings at 10:30 p.m. The Presiding Officer may ask the City Council if any
agenda items listed should be continued or dealt with during the meeting. For those items to be
continued, the City Council can direct the item be placed on the next City Council agenda or the current
meeting may be adjourned to a time certain at which time the meeting shall be reconvened as an
Adjourned Regular Meeting of the City Council and action upon the published agenda continued.

STAFF REPORTS

As a general rule, staff reports. or other written documentation are prepared/organized with respect to
each item of business listed on the agenda. Meeting agendas and staff reports are available at least 72-
hours prior to the scheduled regular City Council meeting and a minimum of 24-hours prior to a Special
City Council meeting. There are times when the City Council receives written material. revised material
after the posting of agendas, these materials are become a public record and will be available for public
view within 72-hours after the meeting in which they were received. Those materials and any other public
document can be inspected in the City Clerk's Office located at 8650 California Avenue, South Gate.

  9
 SERVICES TO FACILITATE ACCESS TO PUBLIC MEETINGS

In compliance with the American with Disabilities Act, if you need special assistance to participate in the
City Council Meetings, please contact the Office of the City Clerk. Notification 48 hours prior to the City
Council Meeting will enable the City to make reasonable arrangements to assure accessibility. For
further information, please contact the Office of the City Clerk at (323) 563-9510 or via email at
yglaze@sogate.org.

SUBJECT:  ORDINANCE  GRANTING  A  FRANCHISE  AGREEMENT  TO  PACIFIC
PIPELINE  SYSTEM,  LLC.,  AND  SETTING  A PUBLIC  HEARING  FOR  MAY  28, 2024

PURPOSE:  To introduce  an ordinance  to grant  a franchise  renewal  to Pacific  Pipeline  System,  LLC.,
("PPS")  for a 10-year  term for an existing  oil pipeline  known  as Pipeline  No. 063 ("Pipeline  063"),  which
were recently  covered  under  Ordinance  No. 2321.  Introduction  of the proposed  ordinance  is the second  of
three actions  required  by the City  Council  to renew  the franchise.

RECOMMENDED  ACTIONS:  Following  the conclusion  of the public  hearing,  the City  Council
will  consider  waiving  the reading  in full  and introducing  an Ordinance  granting  a ten-year  franchise
agreement  to Pacific  Pipeline  System,  LLC.,  to use, maintain,  repair,  and replace  pipelines  beneath
specified  public  streets,  together  with  related  appurtenances,  for transmitting  and distributing  oil and oil
products.

FISCAL  IMPACT:  If the City  Council  adopts the Ordinance  granting  the franchise  agreement,  PPS will
pay the City  a one-time  granting  fee and annual  fees, as summarized  below.

  Annual  Fees  Granting  Fee  Total

  Year  l  $1,100  $12,943  $14,043
  Year  2 to 10  $10,945  *$10,945
  Total  $12,045  $12,943  $24,988
  * Assumes  an annual  CPI iricrease  of 2%.

There will  be an increase  in revenue.  The annual  amount  received  under the previous  franchise  agreement
was $1,000  average  per year for a grand  total  of $21,717  including  the Granting  Fee.  Negotiations  have
increased  that amount  to $1,100  per year plus  an annual  CPI increase  for  a total  estimated  revenue  of
$24,988  inclusive  of a CPI increase  and granting  fee.

The granting  fee is consistent  with  Section  13. 10.010  (Rates - General),  of Chapterl3.  10 (Compensation),
Division  l (Oil,  Gas, and Water  Pipelines),  of Title  13 (Franchises)  of the South  Gate Municipal  Code.
The annual  rate is set in compliance  with  California  Public  Utilities  Code 6231.5  subsection  (e)(2),  which
applies  to utility  pipelines  that are not publicly  owned.  It authorizes  an annual  franchise  fee in an amount

  1

  11
 agreed to by the applicant  and the municipality,  or an aru'iual franchise  fee computed  by multiplying  the
sum of one-half  of the nominal  internal  diameter  of the pipe, expressed in inches, by the number  of lineal
feet of the pipe within  the public  streets, ways, alleys, or other public places within  the municipality.

NOTICINGPROCEDURES:  Before  the  City  Council  can  grant  a Franchise  Agreement,
California  Public  Utility  Code Sections  6232 et seq. requires  a public  hearing.  A public  hearing  notice
was duly published  in The Los Angeles  Wave, a newspaper  of general circulation  on May 2, 2024.

ANALYSIS:  The City regulates utility  companies  that have facilities  that occupy the public  right-of-way
through  franchise  agreements.  The City's  10-year  franchise  with  PPS expired  on April  8, 2024.  PPS
provided  a Letter of Interest to the City on March 11, 2024, stating their interest in renewing  the franchise
agreement  for the pipeline  located on Miller  Way, between Garfield  Avenue  and Vinvale  Terminal,  which
was granted  under Ordinance  No. 2321.  Before  the City  can award a franchise,  the California  Public
Utility Code Section 6232 et seq., requires  the City  Council  to hold a public  hearing  to introduce  an

ordinance granting the franchise agreement.

The proposed Franchise Agreement is identical to the current Franchise Agreement  except for its effective
period, term, and fees. Highlights of the proposed Franchise Agreement include:

  *  Covers Pipeline  No. 063.

  *  A 10-year term from April  9, 2024 to April  8, 2034.

  @  TermsandconditionswhichareinaccordancewithCaliforniaPublicUtilitiesCodeSection620l
  and Ordinance

  *  Pipeline maintenance in accordance  with  all city, county,  state, and federal  ordinances,  statutes,
  rules, regulations, and other laws.

  *  Establishing  liability  insurance,  bond, and indemnity  requirements.

  *  Setting the franchise payment,  and the rules and requirements  under which  the PPS franchise  will
  be required to operate.

  @  Providing  an emergency  response  plan meeting  the requirements  of federal  and state law.  The
  plan must be comprehensive  and provide  a 24-hour  notification  program  and emergency  response

  services,  including  traffic  control,  street excavation,  pipeline  repair,  and supplies  and services  as

  necessary, within two (2) hours of notification  of any problem.  It also requires  repairs  of public
  streets, alleys, or parkways within seventy-two  (72) hours.

  The Pipelines  carry gasoline  and diesel products,  and are the only pipelines  owned by PPS within  the
  City.  The Pipelines  are located  within  500 feet of the residential  and school  zones.  The safety
  standard referenced  in the Franchise  Agreement  requires  the operation  of the Pipelines  in accordance
  with  Government  Code Section  51010. Under this code, the State Fire Marshall  exercises  exclusive
  safety regulatory  and enforcement  authority  over hazardous  liquid  pipelines  and may implement  the
  federal Hazardous  Liquid  Pipeline  Safety Act (49 U.S.C.  Sec. 2001 et seq.) and federal pipeline  safety
  regulations,  as necessary  to obtain  annual  federal  certification.  Thus,  the Pipelines  must be used,
  operated,  repaired,  or modified  in accordance  with  the safety regulations  set by the California  State
  Fire Marshal,  'further, and/or Chief of Los Angeles  Fire Department  in accordance  with Chapter 13.14
  (Special  Provisions  for  Oil  Pipelines),  Division  l  (Oil,  Gas and Water  Pipelines),  of Title  13

  2

  12
   (Franchises)  of the South Gate Municipal  Code. The State Fire Marshal  is further  required  to annually
  inspect  the Pipelines  to ensure  compliance  with  laws  and regulations.  PPS is required  to submit
  certified  test results  for the pipelines  subject  to the provision  of the Pipeline  Safety  Act of 1981.

BACKGROUND:  PPS  owns  and  operates  two  existing  pipelines  in the  City  ("Pipelines").  The
Pipelines  carry  gasoline  and diesel  products  and have been in place since at least 1994.  They  have been
operated  by several  oil and pipeline  companies  under  several  City  franchises.  The Pipelines  are covered
by separate  franchises,  as follows:

  *  Pipeline  No.  063 is covered  under  Ordinance  No.  2321.  This ten-year  ordinance  was adopted  on
  April  9, 2014 and expired  on April  8, 2024.  Pipeline  No. 063 is a 14-inch  diameter,  1/4-mile-long
  pipeline  located  on Miller  Way,  between  Garfield  Avenue  and Vinvale  Terminal.  The pipeline
  services  the Vinvale  Terminal,  which  is a 35-acre  terminal  used to store gasoline  and diesel  fuel
  products  for delivery  by tanker  trucks.

  @  Pipeline  No. 2000 is covered  under  Ordinance  No. 2337. The franchise  expires  on September  13,
  2026.  This  pipeline  is a 20-inch  diameter,  1-mile-long  pipeline  located  on Alameda  Avenue,
  between  Southern  Avenue  and the south City  limit.

The most recent  franchise,  Ordinance  No. 2321,  was adopted  by the City  Council  on April  9, 2014,  and
expired  on April  8, 2024.  PPS has requested  that the franchise  for Pipeline  No. 063 be renewed  for a 10-
year term.  South Gate Municipal  Code,  Section  13.08.010,  allows  the term of the franchise  to be twenty-
five years.  To better  manage  pipelines  within  the City,  it is the practice  of the City to issue franchises  on
a ten-year  term basis in order to ensure  the pipelines  are well  maintained.  The proposed  Resolution  will
extend  the term of the franchise  for an additional  ten years,  cornmencing  retroactively  on April  8, 2024,
and expiring  on April  8, 2034.  Introduction  of the proposed  ordinance  is the second  of three  actions
required  by the City  Council  to renew  the franchise.  The schedule  for issuing  the Franchise  Agreement
is as follows:

  Action  Description  Date
  1  Adopt  a Resolution  declaring  the intention  to grant a franchise  to PPS.  4/23/2024
  2  Conduct  a public  hearing  and- introduce  an ordinance  granting  a ten-
  year franchise  to PPS. At the conclusion  of the public  hearing,  the
  5/28/2024
  City  Council  may overnule,  deny,  or deem insufficient  any oral or
  written  protests,  and may then grant the franchise.

  3  Adopt  the Ordinance  (Franchise)  6/11/2024

Renewal  of the Franchise  Agreement  is recommended  for the reasons  following:

  *  Granting  the Franchise  Agreement  to PPS will  automatically  bestow  rights  upon  the City  and
  create obligations  that must be performed  by PPS for the benefit  of the City,  pursuant  to Article  4
  (Public  Utilities  Code §§ 6291 through  6302)  of California's  Franchise  Act of 1937,  including  the
  following:

  o  The City  shall have the right  to terminate  the franchise  and/or  sue PPS for any failure  to
  properly  perform  PPS's  obligations  under  the franchise.

  3

  13
   o  Requires  PPS to comply  with  ordinances  and policies  adopted  by the City  Council  relative
  to the location  and maintenance  of the Pipeline  and any appurtenances.

  o  Provides  compensation  to the City  for the cost of any repairs  to public  property  made
  necessary  by PPS's  operations  under the franchise.

  o  Requires  PPS to indemnify  and defend  the City  from  and against  damages  resulting  from
  PPS's  operations  under the franchise.

 SUBJECT:  RESOLUTION  ORDERING  THE  LEVY  OF  THE  FISCAL  YEAR  2024/25
 ANNUAL  ASSESSMENT  FOR  THE  STREET  LIGHTING  AND  LANDSCAPING
 MAINTENANCE  DISTRICT  NO.  I

 PURPOSE:  To  adopt  a Resolution  ordering  the  levy  of  the  Fiscal  Year  2024/25  Annual
 Assessment  within  the Street Lighting  and Landscaping  Maintenance  District  No. 1.

 RECOMMENDED  ACTION:  Following  the  conclusion  of  the  public  hearing,  the  City
 Council  will  consider  adopting  a Resolution  ordering  the levy  of the Fiscal  Year 2024/25  Annual
 Assessment  for the Street Lighting  and Landscaping  Maintenance  District  No. 1.

 FISCAL  IMPACT:  The recommended  assessment  levy  is proposed  to remain  the same.  It will
 generate  $1,994,154  for the FY 2024/25.  The assessment  levy has not been changed  since 1993.
 The  costs  associated  with  the  Street  Lighting  and  Landscaping  Maintenance  District  are

 approximately  $3,041,636.  The  deficit  of $1,047,482  is funded  with  Measure  R, Gas Tax  and
 Proposition  A.

 NOTICING  PROCEDURE:  A Public  Hearing  Notice  was duly  published  in the Los Angeles
  Wave, a local  newspaper  of general  circulation,  on May  9, 2024.

 ANALYSIS:  The assessment  amount  is currently  set at $2.38 per adjusted  front  footage.  The
 total  in revenue  produced  from  this assessment  has remained  constant  over the years  while  the
 total  cost of maintaining  the District  has increased,  leaving  an operating  shortfall.  The revenue
 for  FY2024/25  is estimated  to be $1,994,154,  while  the  cost  of  maintaining  the  District  is
 estimated  to be $3,041,636. There  is currently  an operating  budget  deficit  of $1,047,482.  Staff is
 not recommending  increasing  the assessment  levy  at this time.  Any  adjustments  or creation  of a
 new  district/overly  would  be subject  to a Proposition  218 ballot  process  of impacted  property
 owners.

 The  City  Council  has been made  aware  of the deficit  between  revenue  and expenditure.  The
 direction  is to return  at a later date with  an analysis  to review  what  is necessary  to eliminate  the
 deficit.

  1  43
 On April 26, 2016, the City Council authorized a financial analysis to identify alternatives to
minimize the funding deficit which would be needed if the City Council wished to conduct
Proposition 218 Ballot proceedings for new or increased assessments. A consultant conducted
the analysis to determine the feasibility of increasing the assessment within the existing District
to cover the revenue shortfall. Feasible altematives recommended included creating new districts
to supplement the revenue from the subject District. New districts are created via separate and
independent proceedings. As such, as a part of these proceedings, staff is not planning to propose
an increase  to the assessment  rates.

BACKGROUND:  The District was formed in 1981 and operates pursuant to the Landscaping
and Lighting Act of 1972 (California  Streets and Highways Code). The District provides the
authority to levy an assessment on parcels of land which have been identified as receiving  a
direct "special benefit" from a public improvement. The District encompasses  the entire City;
therefore, the assessment is levied on all parcels citywide.

District revenue can only be utilized to meet the original intent of the District:  maintain  and
operate landscaping  and lighting  systems citywide  and within  City streets. Qualifying
expenditures include operations and maintenance of: (a) landscaping (trees, shrubs, grass, other
ornamental vegetation, irrigation  systems and drainage systems) and (b) lighting  systems
(illuminated  signs, decorative light fixtures, street furniture, streetlights and traffic signals),
inclusive  of labor  and materials.

Annually, the District's funds are levied and collected by the Los Angeles County Assessor's
Office (LA County) on behalf of the City in the property tax roll. Several actions from the City
Council are required to provide LA County with the authority to levy and collect the
assessments, according to LA County requirements and applicable state law. The actions before
the City Council are a part of the proceedings necessary to provide such authority.

On February 27, 2024, the City Council adopted Resolution No. 2024-09-CC initiating the
proceedings for FY 2024/25 and directing the Engineers Report to be prepared. On April 22,

  OVERVIEW

  A.  INTRODUCTION

  The City of South Gate (the "City") annually levies and collects special assessments  in
  order to maintain the improvements  within Maintenance  District No. 1 (the "District"). On
  June 22, 1981, the City Council of the City adopted Resolution 3838 which ordered the
  formation of Maintenance  District No.1. The District is levied pursuant to the Landscape
  and Lighting Act of 1972, Part 2 of Division 15 of the California Streets and Highways
  Code (the "1972 Act") and in compliance  with California  Constitution Article XIIID
  ("Article XIIID").

  This Engineer's  Annual  Levy Report  (the "Report")  describes  the District, any
  annexations,  or changes to the District including substantial  changes to the District
  improvements,  and the proposed  assessments  for Fiscal Year 2024/2025.  The
  proposed assessments  are based on the estimated cost to maintain the improvements
  that provide special benefits to properties within the District. The costs of improvements
  and the annual levy include all expenditures,  deficits, surpluses, revenues, and reserves.
  Each parcel is assessed proportionately  for only those improvements  provided and for
  which the parcel receives benefit based on an established method of apportionment.

  The word "parcel," for the purposes of this Report, refers to an individual property
  assigned its own Assessor's Parcel Number by the County of Los Angeles (the "County")
  Assessor's  Office. The County Auditor/Controller  uses Assessor's  Parcel Numbers and
  specific Fund Numbers, to identify on the tax roll, properties assessed for special district
  benefit assessments.

  Following consideration  of public comments  and written protests at a noticed public
  hearing, and review of the Report, the City Council may order amendments  to the Report
  or confirm the Report as submitted.  Following  final approval  of the Report, and
  confirmation  of the assessments,  the Council may order the levy and collection of
  assessments  for Fiscal Year 2024/2025  pursuant to the 1972 Act. In such case, the
  assessment  information will be submitted to the County Auditor/Controller  and included
  on the property tax roll for each benefiting parcel for Fiscal Year 2024/2025.

Ill  METHOD  OF APPORTIONMENT

  A.  GENERAL

  The 1972 Act permits the establishment  of assessment  districts by agencies  for the
  purpose  of providing  certain  public  improvements  that include  the construction,
  maintenance  and servicing  of public lights, landscaping  and appurtenant  facilities.  The
  1972 Act further requires  that the cost  of these  improvements  be levied  according  to
  benefit rather than assessed  value:

  The net amount to be assessed  upon lands within an assessment  district  may be
  apportioned by any formula  or method  which faidy distributes  the net  amount
  among all assessable  lots or parcels in proportion to the estimated  benefits  to be
  received by each such lot or parcel from the improvements.

  The formula  used for calculating  assessments  in this District therefore  reflects  the
  composition  of the parcels,  and the improvements  and services  provided,  to fairly
  apportion  the costs based on benefit to each parcel.

  In addition,  Article  XIIID  requires  that  a parcel's  assessment  may  not  exceed  the
  reasonable  cost of the proportional  special benefit conferred  on that parcel. Article XIIID
  provides  that only special  benefits  are assessable  and the City must separate  the

  B.  BENEFIT  ANALYSIS

  Each of the improvements, the associated costs and assessments within the District has
  been reviewed, identified and allocated based on the special benefit parcels receive
  from such improvements pursuant to the provisions of Article XIIID and the 1972 Act. All
  improvements associated with this District have been identified as necessary, required
  and/or desired for the orderly development of the properties within the District to their
  full potential, consistent with the proposed development  plans. As such, these
  improvements would be necessary and required of individual property owners for the
  development of such properties, and the ongoing operation, servicing and maintenance
  of these improvements would be the financial obligation of those properties. Therefore,
  the improvements  and the annual costs of maintenance  and operation of the
  improvements are of special benefit to the properties.

  All the lots or parcels are established at the same time once the conditions regarding
  the improvements and the continued maintenance are met. As a result, each lot or
  parcel within the District receives a special and distinct benefit from the improvements
  and to the same degree.

  Over time, the improvements continue to confer a particular and distinct special benefit
  upon the lots or parcels within the District because of the nature of the improvements.
  The proper maintenance  of the improvements  and appurtenant facilities reduces
  property related crimes, especially vandalism, against properties in the District. All of
  the above-mentioned  factors also contribute to a specific benefit to each of the parcels
  within the District.

  The method of apportionment (method of assessment) is based on the premise that
  each assessed parcel within the District receives benefit from the improvements.
  However, each individual improvement  element has its own distinct benefits both
  specific and general. The special benefits associated with the improvements within the
  District are as follows:

  Special  Benefit

  The special benefits associated  with the landscaping  improvements  in the District
  are specifically:

  Enhanced  desirability  of  properties  through  association  with  the
  improvements;

  Improved aesthetic appeal of properties providing a positive representation  of
  the area;

  Enhanced adaptation of the urban environment within the natural environment
  from adequate green space, open space areas and landscaping;

  Environmental enhancement through improved  erosion resistance,  dust and
  debris control, and fire prevention;

  C,  ASSESSMENT  METHODOLOGY

  The street lighting, trees, landscaping,  hardscapes,  traffic signals and appurtenant
  facilities are for the benefit and enjoyment of all properties within the District and parcels
  benefit from the operation,  maintenance  and servicing thereof. The assessment  of
  maintenance  and servicing costs upon each parcel is apportioned  in accordance with
  the methodology,  which has been established by the City Council upon formation of the
  District.

  The adjusted front footage of each parcel was determined, at District formation to be the
  most equitable method for spreading the estimated  benefit received by each parcel.
  Lighting, medians, street trees and parkway improvements  are considered "frontage"
  improvements.  The frontage  of a parcel is adjusted  to take into consideration
  configuration,  such as irregular  or corner  parcels,  and whether  a parcel  has
  condominiums  on it.

  D.  MAXIMUM  ASSESSMENT

  In November 1996, voters of the State of California passed Proposition 218 that added
  Articles XIIIC and XIIID to the California  Constitution. Article XIIID requires certain
  noticing, balloting and meeting procedures  For any new or increased  assessment.
  Legislative  changes in the Brown Act defined a "new or increased assessment"  to
  exclude certain conditions. These conditions included "any assessment that does not
  exceed an assessment  formula or range of assessments  previously adopted by the
  agency or approved by the voters in the area where the assessment  is imposed." This
  definition and conditions were later confirmed through Senate Bill 919 (Proposition  218
  implementing  legislation).

  The Maximum Assessment  rate for the District was established  and has remained at
  $2.3789 per adjusted front footage since 1993 and there is no escalation factor approved
  for increasing the Maximum Assessment  rate. The Maximum Assessment  establishes
  a limit on the assessment;  however it does not restrict assessments  to the maximum
  amount. If the budget and assessment  for the Fiscal Year is less than or equal to the
  Maximum  Assessment,  then the required budget and assessment  may be applied
  without additional property owner balloting procedures as required by Article XIIID. If the
  budget and assessments  calculated  require an increase greater than the Maximum
  Assessment,  then the assessment  is considered an increased assessment  and would
  be subject to such balloting procedures.

  contributions.

SUBJECT:  APPEAL  OF PLANNING  COMMISSION  ACTION  REGARDING  ZONING  CODE
  AMENDMENTS

PURPOSE:  To take testimony  and review  evidence  at the appeal hearing,  and decide  whether  to uphold
the Planning  Commission  action,  whether  instead  to reverse  that action  by resolving  to modify  the Zoning
Code;  or take other such action  as may be determined  by the City  Council.

RECOMMENDED  ACTIONS:  Following  the conclusion  of the Public  Hearing,  the City  Council  will
consider:
  a.  Upholding  the action  taken  by  the Planning  Cornrnission  at its April  16,  2024,  meeting,  by
  adopting  a Resolution  attached  hereto;
  b.  Or, in the alternative,  reversing  the Plaru"iing  Commission  action by adopting  a Resolution  attached
  hereto,  which  is a Resolution  of Intent  to adopt an ordinance  amending  the City's  Zoning  Code to
  remove  certain  restrictions  on the size and location  of warehouses  in the City's  Urban  Mixed  Use
  and Commercial  Industrial  zones;  or
  c.  Take other such action  as the City  Council  may determine.

FISCAL  IMPACT:  None

PUBLIC  NOTIFICATION:  Advertising  and notification  of the public  hearing  for  the appeal  was
conducted  in compliance  with  Chapter  11.50.020,  Title  11 of the South  Gate Municipal  Code.  Notice  of
the hearing  was originally  posted  and published  in the "Los  Angeles  Wave"  newspaper  and was mailed  to
surrounding  properties  on May  16, 2024.

ENVIRONMENTALEVALUATION:  UpholdingtheactiontakenbythePlanningCornmissionwould
not affect  CEQA  compliance  Requirements.  Adoption  of a Resolution  Categorically  Exempt  from  CEQA
for two reasons.  First,  amendment  of a zoning  code ordinance  only  constitutes  a "project"  under  CEQA
if it has the potential  for resulting  in direct  or indirect  physical  changes  to the environment,  per 14 CCR  Fg
15378.  This proposed  amendment  will  not cause physical  changes  to the environment,  because  it does
not exempt  future  warehorise  projects  from  Conditional  Use Permit  and CEQA  compliance  requirements.
The proposed  amendment  is therefore  exempt  from  CEQA  because  it does not meet the definition  of a
CEQA  project.  Second,  even if it were to be deemed  a project,  it has no potential  for causing  a significant
effect  on the environment  and is therefore  exempt  from  CEQA  pursuant  to 14 CCR  § 15061.

 BACKGROUND:  At  its  regular  meeting  of  April  16,  2024,  the  City  Planning  Commission
("Commission")  held  a public  hearing  to consider  a Zone  Change  Amendment.  The  Commission
considered  two resolutions  regarding  proposed  changes to Chapter 11.21 of the South Gate Zoning  Code
(which  is set forth in Title 11 of the South Gate Municipal  Code).  The first resolution,  Resolution  No.
2024-02A,  if approved  by the Commission,  recommended  to the City Council  ("Council')  that the City's
Zoning  Code be revised to eliminate  size limitations  on warehouses  in the City's'  Urban Mixed-Use  Zones
and Commercial  Industrial  Zones.  The second resolution,  Resolution  No. 2024-02B,  if approved  by the
Commission,  would  direct the City's  Community  Development  Department  staff ("Staff')  to study the
matter further and return to the Commission  later with recommendations.  The Commission  voted to deny
both resolutions.

ANALYSIS:  The Zoning  Code, together with the City's  General Plan, Specific  Plans and Zoning  Map,
divides  the City into various  geographical  use zones.  Land use permission  tables in Section 11.21.030  of
the Zoning  Code establish  the uses to which  land in each zone may be put.  Table 11.21-3  specifies  uses
allowed  in the Urban  Mixed-Use  Zones, and Table 11.21-4  specifies  uses allowed  in the Commercial
Industrial  zones.  Under  those tables, warehousing  is permitted  (subject  to issuance by the City  of a
Conditional  Use Permit)  in the Industrial  Flex (IF), Light  Industrial  (LF), Light  Manufacturing  (M2) and
Heavy Manufacturing  (M3) zones. However, footnote 18 in Table 11.21-3 and Footnote  11 in Table
11.21-4, each limits the size and placement of warehouses within those zones as follows:

  "Limited  to maximum building area of fifteen thousand  square feet and is not permitted
  along street frontage (would have to be a rear use)."

These footnotes  were incorporated  into the South Gate Municipal  Code in 2015 when the Commission
prepared,  and the Council  enacted,  a comprehensive  update  to the Zoning  Code.  The  Plaru'iing
Commission  and City Council  at that time determined  the inclusion  of these footnotes  was necessary  to
prevent a proliferation  of large warehorises  in the City  which  would  cause detrimental  impacts  to the
community.

Recently,  landowners  and developers  have expressed to the City's  Community  Development  Department
staff  members  (and in some cases to Plaru"iing  Commissioners  and to City  Corincil  Members)  the
landowners'  and developers'  opinions  that the limitations  imposed  by these footnotes  are outdated,  are
unduly  restrictive, and  create  limitations  inconsistent  with  the  current  business  practices  of  the
warehousing industry.

One such developer,  South Gate Owner, LP, and its partners  South Gate GP, LLC  and OMP South Gate
GP LLC  (collectively,  "Appellant"),  whicli  owns  property  in one of the affected  zones,  asked the
Commission  to recommend  to this City  Council  that it amend the Zoning  Code by eliminating  those
footnotes  entirely.  The Cornrnission  conducted  a duly-noticed  public  hearing  to consider  the matter on
April  16, 2024.  After  considering  presentations  by the Community  Development  Department  and by the
Appellant,  and after listening  to public  comments  from  South Gate residents  and business owners both
supporting  and opposing  the requested  change,  the Commission  determined  not to adopt a resolution
recommending  that this  City Council amend the Zoning Code to remove those footnotes  and the
corresponding  restrictions  on the size and location of warehouses in the City ("April 16 Action").

The Appellant  is appealing  the Commission's  April  16 Action  and is asking the City Council  to reverse it

 by adopting  a resolution  of intent  to pass an ordinance  amending  the Zoning  Code  to remove  those
footnotes  and corresponding  restrictions.

CONCLUSION  AND  RECOMMENDATIONS:  The two  resolutions  attached  as exhibits  to this
Agenda  Bill  are mutually  exclusive,  such that only  one, and not both,  should  be adopted  by this  City
Council.

If, after  considering  the presentations  and testimony  presented  at the hearing,  the City  Council  has not
been persuaded  that there is a need to modify  the City's  Zoning  Code to remove  the current  restrictions
on the size and location  of warehouses  within  the City,  then the Council  should  uphold  the Commission's
April  16 Action  by adopting  a Resolution.

But if, after  considering  the presentations  and testimony  presented  at the hearing,  the City  Council  has
been persuaded  that there is a need to modify  the City's  Zoning  Code to remove  the current  restrictions
on the size and location  of warehouses  within  the City,  then the Council  should  reverse  the Planning
Commission's  April  16 Action  by  adopting  a Resolution,  which  is a Resolution  of  Intent  to adopt
Ordinance,  modifying  the City's  Zoning  Code  to remove  footnote  No.  18 from  Table  11.21-3  and to
remove  footnote  No. 11 from  Table  11.21-4.  Alternatively,  the City  Council  can take such other action
as it may determine,  to provide  guidance  to City  Staff.

Coded." (Mun. Code, § 11.52.020.) In order to grant a CUP, the Planning Commission and/or City

  In addition,  all discretionary  projects,  such as those requiring  C{JPs, are subject  to

Resources  Code, § 21080(a).)  The level of environmental  review  under CEQA  generally  depends
on, among other things,  the exact nature of the project  being proposed,  whether  the Site will be
developed  in phases or as a single project,  and whether  the lead agency  detertnines  that an
Environmental  Impact  Report  ("EIR")  is required  rather than a mitigated  negative  declaration
("MND")  or exemption.  Ultimately,  the lead agency - which  in this case would  be the City -
makes the final determination  about whether  an MND,  EIR, or exemption  will  be required  for a
project.

  The CEQA  environmental  review  process - via an A4ND or EIR - is rigorous,  thorough  and
involves  a comprehensive  analysis  of all of a project's  potential  environmental  impacts,  including
traffic,  air quality,  greenhouse  gas, noise, aesthetics,  land use, water and other impact  areas, as well
as suggesting  mitigation  measures that can be imposed  to help reduce or eliminate  any impacts  that
are found to be significant.  As with the C{JP process, and as a second level of review  and "check"
on future warehouse  development,  the City Planning  Commission  and/or City Council  retain
absolute discretion to approve or deny a proposed  warehouse  project  based upon its potential
adverse environmental  impacts.

  Finally,  in the event that a warehouse  project  is approved  by the Planning  Commission  and
involves  some level of public  controversy  or concern,  there is a third level of discretion  and review
in that the Planning  Cornrnission's  action approving  the subject project  can be appealed  by any
interested  party or "opponent"  to the City Council.  (Mun.  Code, § 11.50.040.)  The appeal will  be

fiuther conditions on the pro'3ect beyond those imposed by the Planning Commission in granting the

ANALYSIS:  The  City  regulates  utility  companies  that  have  facilities  that  occupy  the public
right-of-way  through  franchise  agreements.  The  City's  5-year  franchise  with  Tesoro  SoCal  for
the Pipelines  expired  on February  26, 2024.  Tesoro  SoCal  is requesting  renewal  of the franchise
for  the Pipelines  which  was  granted  under  Ordinance  No.  2020-01-CC.  Before  the  City  can
award  a franchise,  the  California  Public  Utility  Code  Section  6232  et seq.,  requires  the City
Council  to adopt  an ordinance  granting  the franchise  agreement.

The  proposed  Franchise  Agreement  is identical  to the current  Franchise  Agreement  with  the
exception  of its effective  period,  term,  and fees. Highlights  of the proposed  Franchise  Agreement
include:

  *  Covers  Pipeline  Nos. 034 and 080.

  *  A 10-year  term from  February  27, 2024, to February  26, 2034.

  *  Terms  and  conditions  which  are in  accordance  with  California  Public  Utilities  Code
  Section  6201 and Ordinance.

  *  Pipeline  maintenance  in accordance  with  all city,  county,  state, and federal  ordinances,
  statutes,  rules, regulations,  and other laws.

  *  Establishing  liability  insurance,  bond,  and indemnity  requirements.

  *  Setting  the  franchise  payment,  and the rules  and  requirements  under  which  the TPC
  franchise  will  be required  to operate.

  *  Providing  an emergency  response  plan meeting  the requirements  of federal  and state law.
  The  plan  must  be  comprehensive  and  provide  a 24-hour  notification  program  and
  emergency  response  services,  including  traffic  control,  street excavation,  pipeline  repair,
  and  supplies  and  services  as necessary,  within  two  (2)  hours  of  notification  of  any
  problem.  It also requires  repairs  of public  streets,  alleys,  or parkways  within  seventy-two
  (72) hours.

 The Pipelines  carry  gasoline  and diesel  products,  and are the only  pipelines  owned  by Tesoro

ensure  compliance  with  laws  and regulations.  Tesoro  SoCal  is required  to submit  certified  test

Garfield  Avenue  and Miller  Way  ending  at the  Vinvale  Terminal  located  at 8601  Garfield
Avenue  ("Pipeline  No. 080").  The Pipelines  carry  gasoline  and diesel  products.

August  26,  2019,  and  expired  on  February  26,  2024.  Tesoro  SoCal  has requested  that  the
franchise  for the Pipelines  be renewed  however  for a 10-year  term.  South  Gate Municipal  Code,

transfer  by BP to Tesoro  Refining  & Marketing  Company  LLC,  a Delaware  limited  liability
company  ("Tesoro  Refining"),  or its affiliates,  of the franchise  granted  by Ordinance  No. 2264;

SoCal,  an affiliate  of Tesoro  Refining,  and Tesoro  SoCal  has owned  and operated  (through  its
affiliate,  Marathon  Pipe Line  LLC,  a Delaware  limited  liability  company)  the Pipelines  since that
time;

26, 2019;

SECTION  1: Definitions.  Whenever  in this Ordinance  the words  or phrases  hereinafter  in this
section  defined  are used, it is intended  that they  shall have the respective  meanings  assigned  to
them in the following  definitions  (unless,  in the given  instance,  the context  wherein  they are used
shall clearly  import  a different  meaning):

  A) The word "City"  shall mean the City  of South  Gate, a municipal  corporation  of the State
  of California,  in its present  incorporated  form  or in any later  reorganized,  consolidated,
  enlarged  or reincorporated  form.
  B)  The word  "Franchise"  shall mean and include  any authorization  by the City  to transmit
  and distribute  thereof  for any and all purposes  under,  along,  across orupon  the public  street,
  ways,  alleys,  and places  in the City  by means  of pipes  and appurtenances  for conducting,
  transporting,  conveying,  and carrying  oil, gas, gasoline,  petroleum,  wet gas, hydrocarbon
  substances,  water,  waste water,  mud and other liquid  substances  for any and all purposes.
  C)  The  word  "Grantee"  shall  mean  Tesoro  SoCal  Pipeline  Company  LLC,  a Delaware
  limited  liability  company,  which  is the entity  to wliom  the Franchise  contemplated  in this
  Ordinance  is granted,  and its lawful  successors  or assigns.
  D)  The phrase "Lay  and Use"  shall mean to lay, construct,  excavate,  erect, install,  operate,
  maintain,  use, repair,  replace,  relocate  or remove.

SECTION  2: Grant  of Franchise.  The right,  privilege  and franchise,  subject  to all terms  and
conditions  contained  in this Ordinance,  and pursuant  to the provisions  of the Division  3, Chapter
2 of the California  Public  Utilities  Code, la'iown  as the Franchise  Act of 1937,  is hereby  granted  to
Grantee,  to  use  a system  of  Pipelines  and  Appurtenances  for  the  purpose  of  conducting,
transporting,  conveying  and  carrying  oil,  gas,  gasoline,  petroleum,  wet  gas,  hydrocarbon
substances,  water,  waste water,  mud and other liquid  substances  under and across the City's  right-
of-way  upon the terms  and conditions  set forth  in Section  3, below.  The City  acknowledges  that
the two Pipelines  identified  above  have already  been installed  within  the City  of South  Gate; the
City  expressly  agrees that the right  to install,  operate,  maintain,  use, repair,  replace,  relocate  and
remove those  Pipelines  is included  among  the rights  granted  in this  Ordinance  as part  of the
Franchise.

SECTION  3: Conditions.  The rights  granted  herein  shall  be subject  to (a) the terms  and
conditions  set forth  in this Ordinance,  and (b) construction  of Pipelines  and Appurtenances  by the
Grantee,  at the Grantee's  expense  and at such time  or times as directed  by the City.

SECTION  4: Term.  The  Franchise  shall  be  for  a term  of  ten  (10)  years  commencing
retroactively  on February  27, 2024  and expiring  on February  26, 2034,  or until  such earlier  time
that:

  A) The Franchise  is voluntarily  surrendered  or abandoned  by  the  Grantee,  or  assigned,
  transferred,  sold  or leased  without  the prior  express  written  consent  of the City,  which
  assignment  shall not be unreasonably  withheld;  or
  B) The State of California,  the City,  or some other municipal  or public  entity  duly  authorized
  by  law  shall  purchase  the  Franchise  area,  as described  in  Section  1(B)  by  voluntary
  agreement,  or shall  condemn  and take  the Franchise  area under  the power  of eminent
  domain;  or the Franchise  is forfeited  by the Grantee  due to the Grantee's  noncompliance
  with  the terms  and conditions  of the Franchise.
  C) The Grantee  shall,  within  thirty  (30) days after the passage of this Ordinance  granting  the
  Franchise,  file with  the City  Clerk  a written  acceptance  of the terms  and conditions  of this
  Ordinance:  provided,  liowever,  that  as to  franchises  granted  to the  United  States  of
  America,  use will  constitute  acceptance.

SUBJECT:  RESOLUTION  DECLARING  A  CONTINUED  EMERGENCY  AND
AUTHORIZING  REPAIR,  REPLACEMENT  OR  MAINTENANCE  ACTIVITIES  OF
PUBLIC  FACILITIES  RELATED  TO  THE  URBAN  ORCHARD,  CITY  PROJECT  NO.
539-PRK  WITHOUT  PUBLIC  BIDDING,  PURSUANT  TO  THE  EMERGENCY
CONTRACTING  PROCEDURES  OF  THE  SOUTH  GATE  MUNICIPAL  CODE  AND
THE  CALIFORNIA  PUBLIC  CONTRACT  CODE

PURPOSE:  To declare  an emergency  still  exists  and to authorize  the repair,  replacement  or
maintenance  activities  of public  facilities  related  to the Urban  Orchard  Project  without  public
bidding.  The  Los  Angeles  County  Department  of  Public  Health,  Solid  Waste  Division
("County")  issued  a Corrective  Action  Order  requiring  construction  to stop on the project.  The
declaration  of  emergency  is necessary  to  streamline  the  process  to  procure  a replacement
contractor  to provide  maintenance  activities  to preserve  the site  in a safe condition  until  the
County  authorizes  construction  work  on the project  to resume.

RECOMMENDED  ACTIONS:  The City  Council  will  consider  making  a finding  and adopting
a Resolution  declaring  an  emergency  still  exists  and  authorizing  repair,  replacement  or
maintenance  activities  of public  facilities  related  to the Urban  Orchard,  City  Project  No.  539-
PRK,  without  public  bidding,  pursuant  to the emergency  contracting  procedures  of the South
Gate Municipal  Code and the California  Public  Contract  Code.

FISCAL  IMPACT:  There  is no  impact  to  the  General  Fund.  The  Urban  Orchard  Project
("Project")  has received  a total  of $30.5 million  in grant and other funds  for design,  construction,
operations,  and maintenance,  as summarized  below.

ANALYSIS:  The Project  was under  construction  and approximately  90% of construction  work
has been  completed.  On  December  29,  2022,  the  City  received  a Corrective  Action  Order
("Order")  from  the County.  The Order  required  the City  to stop all construction  activities  until
such a time  as a Post Closure  Land Use Plan ("PCLUP")  for the Project  site was approved  by the
County.  Given  the PCLUP  approval  process  and  input  received  to date,  it will  take  at least
several months,  possibly  six or more,  to obtain  approval.

To  avoid  the  significant  delay  damages  that  would  be payable  by  the  City  to the  general
contractor  during  a prolonged  suspension  of the project  pending  approval  of the PCLUP,  the City

  1
  147
 Council  terminated  the general  contractor's  agreement  at a Special  City  Council  meeting  on
February  6, 2023.  Such termination  provided  both  immediate  and long-term  cost savings  to the
City  but also created  an immediate  need for the City  to retain  an interim  contractor  to perform
certain  ongoing  maintenance  and safety  activities;  a need which  must  be met  sooner  than  the
time necessary  to engage in normal  public  bidding  procedures

The proposed  Resolution  declares  a continued  emergency  exists pursuant  to the authority  granted
by South  Gate Municipal  Code  § 1.54.470  and California  Public  Contract  Code  § 22050.  Those
Code  Sections  allow  cities,  by resolution,  to approve  the City's  entry  into  contracts  without
engaging  in public  bidding  where  certain  emergency  conditions  are found  to have occurred.  Staff
continues  to believe  that the County's  Order  directing  all construction  work  to be ceased on the
Project,  constitutes  such an emergency  due to the public's  safety  with  an unfinished  construction
site and the need to respond  accordingly  to additional  directives  given  by the County  related  to
ensuring  public  safety.  Staff  are recommending  that  the  City  Council  adopt  the  proposed
Resolution  so that the City  can avail  itself  of the accelerated  contracting  procedures  authorized
by those  Code  Sections.  The  Resolution,  (1)  declares  an emergency,  (2)  authorizes  the City
Manager  to  take  such  actions  deemed  necessary  to  cause  the  maintenance  activities  to  be
performed  and to procure  the necessary  equipment,  services,  and supplies  all  without  giving
notice  for bids for contracts,  (3) requires  that at each regularly  scheduled  City  Council  Meeting,
the  City  Manager  present  to the  Council  the reasons  justifying  why  the emergency  will  not
permit  a delay  resulting  from  a competitive  solicitation  for bids, why  that action  is necessary  to
respond  to the emergency,  and that the City  Council  review  the emergency  action  to determine,
by a four-fifth's  vote,  that there  is a need to continue  the emergency  action  until  the emergency
action  is terminated.

BACKGROUND:  The Project  is a part of the FY 2022/23  Capital  Improvement  Program.  The
Project  is located  between  the Los  Angeles  River,  Firestone  Boulevard,  the Thunderbird  Villa
Mobile  Home  Park, and the I-710  Freeway.  The two primary  purposes  of the Project  are to divert
and treat  storm  water  run-off  from  the Los Angeles  River  and to install  a new park  to provide
riverfront  recreational  opportunities.

The Project  is being  constructed  on a property  that was used as an unpermitted  landfill  until  1949
by an entity  known  as Southeastern  Disposal  and By-Products.  The property  site is identified  in
CalRecycle's  Solid  Waste  Information  System  ("SWIS")  as an Unpermitted  Closed  Solid  Waste
Disposal  Site and SWIS  No. 19-AA-5545.  In 1984,  the State of California  Department  of Health
Services,  Toxic  Substances  Control  Division  concluded  that  the  clean-up  work  completed
effectively  mitigated  waste  constituents  to  proceed  with  the  Lewis  Homes  residential
development  project.  The  requirements  of the PCLUP  came  into  effect  in 1988.  As such,  the
project  site is subject  to State solid  waste regulations  that require  the PCLUP  before  any change
to the current  land use, construction,  or land preparation  can occur.

The Los Angeles  County  Department  of Public  Health,  Solid  Waste  Management  Program,  acts
as the  LEA  for  the  State  of  California's  Department  of Resources  Recycling  and Recovery
("CalRecycle").  The  County  is  authorized  by  Division  30  of  the  Public  Resources  Code
("PRC"),  Section  43209  and 45000,  Title  14 and 27 of the California  Code  of Regulations  (14
CCR  & 27 CCR),  to enforce  applicable  solid  waste  regulations  and to ensure  solid  waste  sites
meet  the  state minimum  standards  within  the  County  of Los  Angeles.  As  such,  the  City  is
working  with  the LEA  to obtain  approval  of the PCLUP.

Construction  is  currently  at  the  90%  completion  stage.  Improvements  that  have  been
substantially  completed  include,  but are not limited  to, rough  grading,  drop inlet  for storm  water
diversion  structures  in the Bandini  Channel,  a wetland  overlook  area, the stream  adjacent  to the
education/flexible  space  building  and  wetland,  south  bio  swale,  construction  of  18  raised
planters,  planting  of  75  trees,  installation  of  the  prefabricated  education  center  and  the
restroorn/maintenance  building,  two  shade  structures,  a water  element  at  the  playground,
installation  of multi-use  walking  and bicycle  pathways,  exercise  equipment  located  at various
stages along the walking  and bicycle  paths,  benches,  picnic  tables,  drinking  fountains,  trash cans,
and pathway  lighting.  Construction  of the project  will  resume  after  the  County  approves  the
CPLUP.

 BACKGROUND:  On their East end, Southern Avenue and Southern Place front South Gate Park
and the LADWP utility corridor. These areas have limited visibility from the general public as
compared to streets in residential neighborhoods and are therefore used for overnight parking.
Overnight parking activity is a concern. The Los Angeles Fire Department Station 54 is located at
the intersection of Southern Avenue and Southern Place. Fire Department personnel at that station
requested that the City prohibit street parking onthe portion of Southern inthe vicinity ofthe station,
citing concerns over vehicle break-ins. Also, the City is informed that homes just east of the Fire
Station have evening and overnight issues with people parking on Southern Avenue, south of their
homes. A resident requested a preferential parking district; however, that would not be allowed by
the municipal code, because it is not in a residential community. Finally, the Parks and Recreation
Department also cited issues with overnight parking adjacent to the South Gate Park due to related
activities.

Staff recommends that overnight parking be prohibited from 11:00 P.M. to 7:00 A.M. as means to
resolve the issues. This solution balances the competing needs of South Gate residents relative to
limited parking availability, access to the adjacent City park, and public safety. It was ultimately
determined that a complete prohibition  on parking in that vicinity was not necessary,  and that

  PURPOSE:  To approve  the update  to the job  specification  for the full-time  Housing  Assistant
  position  in the Community  Development  Department.

  RECOMMENDED  ACTIONS:  The City  Council  will  consider  adopting  a Resolution  amending

  tlie classification  specification  for the full-time  position  of Housing  Assistant  in the Cornrnunity
  Development  Department.

  ANALYSIS:  None.

  BACKGROUND:  TheCitymust,fromtimetotime,add,remove,reclassify,orotherwiseadjust
  job  classifications,  job  specifications  and/or  compensation  in the Salary  Resolution  and Position
  Classification  Plan in order to satisfy  the changing  needs and demands  of the City's  workforce.  In

  to more  closely  match  the tasks which  need to be performed  by employees  in the City's  various
  departments

  On April  23, 2024, the City  Council  approved  the reclassification  of one of the full-time  Housing
  Specialist  positions  to a Housing  Assistant  position  in an effort  to find  quality  applicants  to assist
  the City's  Housing  Authority.  This new position  will  permit  the City to hire a promising  candidate
  that does not have the necessary  Housing  Certifications  to qualify  as a Housing  Specialist  and then
  provide  that employee  with  the opportunity  to obtain  the necessary  certifications  during  his/her
  first  year of employment.  Once that individual  has obtained  the necessary  certifications  and has
  some  experience  in the City's  Housing  Authority,  he/she  will  then be an ideal  candidate  to be
  promoted  into a vacant  Housing  Specialist  position.  This  entry-level  position  allows  the Housing

 Authority  the flexibility  to hire  a promising  candidate  and then train  that person.  However,  the
minimum  certification qualifications  approved  for the Horising  Assistant  position  are inadvertently
higher than that of the Housing  Specialist.

Specifically,  the certifications  required  for the Housing  Specialist  are "Possession  of at least two
(2) Housing  Certifications  with[in]  18 montlis  of hire date is required."  However,  the minimum
certifications  qualifications  for Housing  ASSiStant as approved  on April  23, 2024, are "Possession
of the Housing  Choice  Voucher  (HCV)  Specialist  Certificate  and one of the following  certificates
within  one (l)  year of hire is required  to successfully  pass probation..."

In an effort  to correct  this oversight  and ensure that the minimum  certification  qualifications  for

to the Housing  Assistant  job  classification  is requested:  "The  following  two  certifications  are
required  within  eighteen  (18)  months  of hire  to successfully  pass probation:  Possession  of the
Housing  Choice  Voucher  (HCV)  Specialist  Certificate  and one of the following  certificates..."

Human  Resources  staff worked  with  the Community  Development  Department  to develop  the job
classification  specifications  for the Housing  Assistant.  Staff also worked  with  MEA  to review  the
new job  specifications  and the recommended  pay, of which  they agree.

  SUBJECT:  RESOLUTION  DENOUNCING  DIGIT  AL  DISCRIMINATION

  PURPOSE:  To consider  the adoption  of a Resolution  that:

  1.  Denounces  digital  discrimination  and commits  to addressing  the disparate  outcomes  of
  provider  decisions  that impact  access to broadband  internet  based on income  level,  race,
  ethnicity,  color,  religion,  or national  origin;  and
  2.  Urges  internet  service  providers  to provide  fast, reliable,  and affordable  internet  to all
  communities  regardless  of income  level,  race, ethnicity,  color,  religion,  or national  origin;
  and
  3.  Encourages  its residents  to report  all acts of digital  discrimination  to the Federal
  Coinmunications  Commission  (FCC),  the Public  Advocates  Office  of the California  Public
  Utilities  Coi'nmission  (CPUC),  and Supervisor  Janice  Hahn,  with  the Los Angeles  County
  Board  of Supervisors;  and
  4.  Supports  efforts  to close the digital  divide  and ensure  digital  equity  for all residents.

  RECOMMENDED  ACTIONS:  Adopt  the Resolution  denouncing  digital  discrimination.

  FISCAL  IMPACT:  There  is no fiscal  impact  ori the General  Fund.

  ANALYSIS:  The City  of South  Gate recognizes  the critical  importance  of broadband  internet  access
  for full  participation  in modern  society  and that digital  discrimination  occurs  when  internet  service
  providers  (ISPs)  inequitably  deploy  high-speed  internet  connections  or disproportionately  withhold
 the best deals for their  services  froin  racially  or socio-economically  marginalized  neighborhoods.

  Studies  have shown  that providers  systematically  offer  worse  service  - slower,  delivered  over older
 technology  - to low-income  coininunities  at a higher  price  that they offer  fast, reliable  service  to
  higlier  incoi'ne  coi'nmunities  and digital  discritnination  exacerbates  the challenge  of affordability  and
  worsens  the digital  divide.

 BACKGROUND:  In Noveinber  2023,  the Federal  Coi'ni'nunications  Coi'nmission  (FCC)  codified
  rriles to prevent  digital  discrin'iination,  outlining  a coi'nplaint  process  wliereby  ineinbers  of the public
 cai'i  offer  evidence  of digital  discriinination  being  coininitted  by Internet  service  providers  (ISPs).
 The FCC  has defii'ied  digital  discrimination  as "Policies  or practices,  not justified  by genuine  issues

  168
 of technical  or econoi'nic  feasibility,  that (1) differentially  impact  consui'ners'  access to broadband
internet  access service  based on their  income  level,  race, ethnicity,  color,  religion,  or national  origin
or (2) are intended  to have such differential  impact".

Closing  the digital  divide  and ensuring  equitable  access to fast, reliable,  and affordable  internet  is
necessary  for accessing  education,  health  care, and participating  in economic  oppoitunities  and civic
life.

and

  WHEREAS,  closing  the digital  divide  and ensuring  equitable  access to fast, reliable,  and
affordable  internet  is necessary  for accessing  education,  health  care, and participating  in
economic  opportunities  and civic  life.

NOW,  THEREFOR,  THE  CITY  COUNCIL  OF  THE  CITY  OF  SOUTH  GATE,
CALIFORNIA,  DOES  HEREBY  RESOLVE  AS FOLLOWS:

disparate  outcomes  of provider  decisions  that impact  access to broadband  internet  based on
income  level,  race, ethnicity,  color,  religion,  or national  origin.

SECTION  2. The City  Council  urges internet  service  providers  to provide  fast, reliable,  and
affordable  internet  to all communities  regardless  of income  level,  race, ethnicity,  color, religion,
or national  origin.

SECTION  3. The City  Council  encourages  its residents  to report  all acts of digital
discrimination  to the Federal  Coinmunications  Commission  (FCC),  the Public  Advocates  Office

 ANALYSIS:  The South  Gate Park  Sports  Center  HVAC  Project  (Project)  is under  design  and
scheduled  to begin  construction  in late 2024.  The goal is to complete  construction  in mid-2025
prior  to the 2025 summer  season.  The Project  requires  replacing  the HVAC  system which  includes
installing  a 130-ton  chiller.  The procurement  of the chiller  has an estimated  lead time of 42 weeks.
To stay on schedule,  staff purchased  the chiller  in advance  of awarding  a construction  contract  to
ensure  it is readily  available  for installation  during  construction.  The chiller  is scheduled  to be
delivered  in July 2024,  well  before  the project  begins  construction.  With  the early delivery  of the
chiller,  staff is now planning  to complete  the project  in two separate  construction  phases.  Phase I
includes  installation  of  the  pre-purchased  chiller,  and  Phase  II  includes  installation  of  the
remaining  HVAC  appurtenances.  The current  Project  design  is now at the 90 percent  completion
level.  However,  these design  and construction  documents  include  a requirement  for the contractor
to procure  and install  the chiller.  As such, the current  design  documents  need to be revised  to
remove  the purchase  and installation  of the chiller  from  design  documents  so that the project  can
be implemented  in two  phases.  Accordingly,  Amendment  No.  1 to Contract  No.  2023-99-AC
provides  $30,000  to revise  the design  plans.

The engineer's  estimate  for the project  requires  a budget  of $1,411,291  to complete  design  and
construction.  To date, a total of $211,291  in Rendon  2023 the State of California  Grant  Funds  has
been budgeted,  thus an additional  $1.2 Million  is required.

BACKGROUND:  The existing  HVAC  System  at the Sports  Center  needs major  maintenance
repairs.  Its chiller  system  fails regularly  as it is undersized  and near the end of its service  life.  Due
to it being  undersized,  it shuts down  regularly  during  the hot summer  months  when  demand  is
high.  It provides  inadequate  cooling  when  the  outside  air  temperature  exceeds  85 degrees
Fahrenheit.  Further,  it does not provide  adequate  cooling  to maintain  comfortable  temperatures  in
the two  weight  rooms.  Last summer  season,  a temporary  back-up  system  was rented  to provide
cooling,  which  will  be rented  again this summer  season at an estimated  cost of $25,000  monthly.
The Sports  Center  HVAC  Project  is being  implemented  to make the necessary  HVAC  repairs  and
improvements.

On July  10, 2023,  the City  Manager  approved  Contract  No.  2023-99-AC  with  EDA,  to prepare
design  and construction  documents  for the Project,  in the amount  of $49,900.  Amendment  No. 1
to Contract  No.  2023-99-AC  provides  $30,000  for  additional  services,  for  a revised  contract
amount  of  $79,900.  Services  include  administration,  design,  and technical  support  through
construction  completion.

Proceeding  with  the project  in two  phases  has benefits.  Mainly,  it provides  for the permanent
installation  of the  chiller  to meet  the  demand  for  cooling  the  Sports  Center  to comfortable
temperatures  with  permanent  equipment.  It also reduces  costs since the rental  equipment  will  be
eliminated.

The  design  and construction  documents  are at the 90%  completion  stage.  The chiller  will  be
installed  by October  2025.  Construction  of the project  is planned  to start in early 2025.

STATEMENT  OF UNDERSTANDING  / TECHNICAL  APPROACH

The project at hand is for substantial refit of HVAC services serving the South Gate Sports Center. Specific
components of this refit include the replacement of the chiller and supplemental capacity for new equipment for
airside HVAC services to locker rooms and weight rooms. There are various components outboard of the scope
such as the gymnasium air handling unit (to include economizer exhaust) and air handlers otherwise, hot water
services (to include heating hot water, domestic hot water, pool heating, and cogeneration), rooftop package
equipment in vicinity and on second floor services (deemed "available for reconfiguration as part of this project',
but bears review for applicability), and pool ventilation. Consideration as part of this project would lend to controls
as new controls could be developed for expansion, to be extended to balance of systems new thereafter.

The chiller is air cooled, and 110 tons in capacity. The unit is undersized and at end of service life. It is noted
that the record drawings reflect two 65 ton chillers rather than the singular 110 ton chiller, and these terms bear
consideration as design for replacement is reconciled. It is a primary purpose of this project to replace the chiller.
Inherent consideration is for replacement of pumping services (and potential upgrade to duplex pumping for
redundancy), and refit of piping as is deemed necessary and/or appropriate. Consideration on that account is to
minimize work where possible, and redevelop services as justified and agreed upon. Among issues to consider
as part of the design effort include the weight of equipment and capacity of structure to bear any increases in
weight, necessary upgrades to electrical services, and adequacy of piping for size and condition as noted above.

There are multiple air handlers serving two weight rooms and two locker rooms. The equipment is serviceable,
but inadequate in size, and for expanded spaces served. These units have 10 years (+ / -) of service life
remaining,  Consideration  is for those appropriate opportunities to displace services from the existing
installations, and to provide new services supplemental to the existing. Design considerations would include
equipment locations, capacity for economizer services, maintenance  of existing elements, and strategic
placement and intercept and merge and meld of new and existing equipment. Specific consideration would be to
locate new equipment on the roof over the weight rooms and the locker rooms. Additional consideration would be
to reconfigure the existing rooftop package units thereabouts and above the weight rooms and lockers. This
Consultant understands the preference by Owner to re-purpose the existing package equipment and has advised
client of opportunities and fallibilities as to the proposition. Issues to consider as part of the design effort include
the weight of equipment and capacity of structure to bear any increases in weight (a lesser degree, for the
weights involved herewith, measures for electrical services, and modifications to piping to accommodate the
proposed measures for upgrade.

This Consultant also understands the Owner's intent to maintain the Scope of Work to "tasks at hand" for the
equipment replacement cited herein. Preliminary budget costs by the Consultant is upwards of $400,000 or more
(and depending on the ultimate Scope of Work), and these terms are noted to the Owner.

Whereas these types of installations would entail microprocessor based controls (i.e. DDC, BAS), it is understood
and / or expected that there are no such controls in this facility. Options on this account include: 1) develop
upgrades for current generation BAS as part of this design for extent of services as agreed upon, and with
capacity for expansion in due time to integrate balance of services at this facility onto the upgraded controls
platform; or 2) integrate the new equipment into the existing controls hierarchy (deemed an unlikely decision; or
3) to design this project for controls stand alone and on a component by component basis. This decision can be
made in the course of design.

A specific consideration worth noting herein is that the gym air handier is substantial in capacity and
configuration, and with limited effort could be revitalized for good function, to include the economizer service.
Whereas this task is outboard of the scope as is identified as part of the RFP, it bears discussions as terms of the
project are finalized.

PURPOSE:  To award  a Professional  Services  Agreement  to Golden  Meters  Service,  Inc., to meet
the requirements  of the US EPA's  Lead and Copper  Rule Revisions  (LCRR)  by identifying  water
service  line material  from  the meter  to the customers  building  inlet.

RF,COMMENDED  ACTIONS:  The City  Council  will  consider:
  a.  ApprovingaProfessionalServicesAgreementwithGoldenMetersService,Inc.,toprovide
  services  to complete  the Lead  and Copper  Rule  Revisions,  City  Project  No.  724-WTR  as
  necessary  to meet new Federal  requirements,  in an amount  not-to-exceed  $683,000;
  b. Appropriating  $683,000  in Water  Funds to fully  fund the Lead and Copper  Rule Revisions,
  City  Project  No. 724-WTR;  and
  c.  Authorize  the Mayor  to execute  the Agreement  in a form  acceptable  to the City  Attorney.

FISCAL  IMPACT:  There  is no impact  to the General  Fund.  The Proposed  Agreement  and the
proposed  appropriation  are both in the amount  of $683,000  recommended  to be :tunded with  Water
Funds.

ANALYSIS:  The US EPA's  LCRR  requires  all California  community  water  systems  to develop
and submit  a water  service  line material  inventory  to the Division  of Drinking  Water  (DDW)  by
October  16, 2024.  The purpose  of the inventory  is to confirm  the existence  of led service  lines.
The City  conducted  an inventory  of service  lines  material  in 2020,  on public  property  from  the
water  mains  to the water  meter  and did not find  any lead pipes.  The LCRR  now requires  the City
to conduct  an inventory  on customer-owned  services  (private  property)  from  the meter  to the
building  inlet.  The  inventory  must  include  all  service  lines  connecting  the water  main  to the
building  inlet,  regardless  of  ownership  status  and  intended  use.  Each  service  line  must  be
categorized  as one of the following:  Lead,  Non-lead  (copper,  plastic,  etc.) Galvanized  requiring

replacement  (GRR).  The City  is also required  to post the inventory  online  and include  instructions
on how to access the inventory  online  through  the annual  Consumer  Confidence  Report.  Further,
the City must noti:ty  customers  and discuss  a replacement  plan if a lead service  line is found  serving
their property.

 The Public Works Department does not have the staffing resources to complete this effort.  As
such, it is recommended that a contract be awarded to Golden Meters, Inc. (GM), to complete  the
project

BACKGROUND:  The City's water system has approximately 135 miles of water mains. It
serves the majority of City except for a portion of the Hollydale area, via over 14,400 service
connections to residential, commercial, and industrial customers. Based on the EPA's new
requirements, a total of 12,500 service connections will be required to be inventoried to confirm
the presence of led. The remaining services connections will not be included in the project as they
were constructed a:[ter 1986, which is after lead pipes were banned from use in 1985.

Staff prepared a Request For Proposal (RFP) and issued on March 12, 2024. The City received
one proposal on April 2, 2024 in the amount of $683,000, from Golden Meters Service, Inc. and
is recommended for the contract. Located in Fullerton, Golden Meters, Inc. (GM), has over 14
years of experience in the water industry and is qualified to perform lead inspections.  GM has
serviced over 100 water agencies throughoutthe State and has annual testing agreements and meter
replacement contracts with over 50 agencies. GM has the needed experience to complete the
project.

The proposal includes physical visual inspections of the estimated 12,500 service connections,
which will include cleaning the meter box and taking a photo of the service line, as well the
building inlet, documenting on the City's GIS so'[tware, and verifying metal pipes.

EPA is proposing the Lead and Copper Rule Improvements (LCRI) to significantly  reduce
exposure to lead through drinking water. The proposal builds on the 2021 Lead and Copper Rule
Revisions (LCRR) to the 1991 Lead and Copper Rule (LCR). The proposed LCRI strengthens key
elements  of the rule in three main  focus  areas:

  *  Identifying  and Replacing  Lead Service  Lines.
  *  Reducing  Complexity  and Improving  Public  Health  Protection.
  *  Increasing  Transparency  and Informing  the Public.

B,  Definition  of a lead service  line, gooseneck  and galvanized  }ine

  11 Lead service line means a portion of pipe that is made of lead, which connects the
  water main to the building inlet, A lead service line may be owned by the water
  system, owned by the property owner, or both, A galvanized setvice line is
  considered a lead service line, or a "galvanized requiring replacement" (C3RR), line

  pigtail, or connector, and it is not a galvanized service line that is considered a lead
  service line, then the service line is not a lead service line.

The United  States  Environmental  Protection  Agency  (u.s. EPA) issued revisions to the federal
Lead and Copper  Rule (LCR)  on January  15, 2021.  u.s. EPA's new Lead and Copper Rule
Revisions  (LCRR)  strengthen  every  aspect  of the LCR to better  protect  communities  and
children  in elementary  schools  and childcare  facilities  from the impacts  of lead exposure.  The
new LCRR  will get the lead out of our nation's  drinking  water  and empower  communities
through  information.  Over the next three  years,  the LCRR  will require  community  water
systems  (CWSs)  and non-transient  non-community  water  systems  (NTNCs)  throughout  the
United  States  (approximately  4,000  water  systems  in California)  to conduct  an inventory  of
service  lines and determine  the material  of those  lines and fittings.

On January  20, 2021,  federal  Executive  Order 13990  directed  all federal  agencies  to
undertake  review  and action,  as appropriate,  to address  the promulgation  of federal
regulations  and other  actions  during  the prior four years.  Of those  actions,  the LCRR  was
specifically  identified  as an agency  action  requiring  review.  Consequently,  u.s. EPA delayed
the effective  and compliance  dates  established  in the LCRR  to December  16, 2021 and
October  16, 2024,  respectively.  u.s. EPA also engaged  with local communities,  states,  local
governments,  utilities,  and stakeholders  for input regarding  any changes  that should  be made
to the LCRR.

On December  I 6, 2021,  following  u.s. EPA engagement  activities,  U.S EPA published  Docket
No. EPA-HQ-OW-2021-0255  in the federal  register.  The LCRR  compliance  and effective
dates  listed above,  as well as the text from the January  15, 2021  regulation,  were  not changed
and became  effective.  Within  the Docket,  u.s. EPA committed  to propose  and revise  the
LCRR  by October  2024 with the Lead and Copper  Rule Improvements  (LCRI).  The LCRI are

1. What  are the new requirements  and what  must  be included  in the LSL Inventory
under  the LCRR?

All community  and non-transient  non-community  public water  supply  systems  (water  systems)
must comply  with the LCRR.  Water  systems  must develop  an inventory  to identify  service  line
materials  connected  to the public  water  distribution  systems  by October  I 6, 2024.  Though  the
LCRR  do not define  a "service  line," they define  a "lead  service  line" as such: "Lead  service
line means  a portion  of pipe that is made  of lead, which  connects  the water  main to the
building  inlet. ..." (Complete  definition  in Section  2). The inventory  must include  all service
lines connected  to the water  system's  distribution  system,  regardless  or ownership  status.  Ita
the service  line ownership  is shared,  the inventory  would  include  both the portion  of the service
line owned  by the water  system  and the customer-owned  portion  of the service  line.

2. What  is the LCRR  definition  of a lead service  line,  gooseneck  and galvanized  line?

Lead service  line means  a portion  of pipe that is made of lead, which  connects  the water  main
to the building  inlet. A lead service  line may be owned  by the water  system,  owned  by the
