Section 4), line if it ever was or is currently downstream  of any lead service line or service  line
of unknown material. If the only lead piping serving the home is a lead gooseneck,  pigtail, or
connector, and it is not a galvanized service line that is considered a lead service line, then the
service line is not a lead service line.

Gooseneck, piqtail, or fittinq, connector is a short section of piping, typically not exceeding two
feet, which can be bent and used for connections between rigid service piping. Lead
goosenecks,  pigtails, fittings, and connectors  are not considered  to be lead service lines but
must be replaced when encountered during planned or unplanned infrastructure  work pursuant
to 40 Code of Federal Regulation (CFR) section 141.84, subdivision (c).

Galvanized service line means iron or steel piping that has been dipped in zinc to prevent
corrosion and rusting.

Note from the LCRR definitions  above;  A galvanized  line that is connected  downstream  of
a lead gooseneck,  pigtail, fitting, or connection is not considered  a GRR and does not require

3. How are the general  requirements  in California  Health  and  Safety  Code  section
116885  and  the  LCRR  similar?

California Health and Safety Code section 116885-Lead  Service Lines in Public  Water

Sess., Stats. 2016, ch. 731 ) and amended by Senate Bill No. 427 (2017-2018  Reg. Sess.,
Stats. 2017, ch. 238), required all community water systems (CWSs) to compile an inventory of
known partial or total lead user service lines in use in their distribution systems by July 1, 2018.
The submission deadline for the final user service line inventory was July 1, 2020.

The definition of "user service line" in the California Health and Safety Code2 includes  the
service line from the water main to the meter, which is typically the water-system-owned
portion of the line. Health and Safety Code section 116885 requires that all lead from the
water main to the meter be inventoried  and replaced. The State Water Resources  Control
Board's (State Water Board) Division of Drinking Water (DDW) will continue to collect data on
lead goosenecks  and required service line replacement  plans. Water systems that reported

4. How  is each  portion  of the service  line material  categorized  in the LCRR?

DDW will be collecting  material  data on both the water-system-owned  portion  of the service
line (water  main to the meter)  and the customer-owned  portion  of the service  line (meter  to the
building  inlet).  Each  portion  of all service  lines served  by all water  systems  must be
categorized  in the following  manner:

  (i) "Lead"  where  the service  line is made of lead.

  (ii) "Galvanized  Requiring  Replacement"  (GRR)  where  a galvanized  service  line is or was
at any time downstream  of a lead service  line or is currently  downstream  of a "Lead  Status
Unknown"  service  line. If the water  system  is unable  to demonstrate  that the galvanized
service  line was never  downstream  of a lead service  line, it must presume  there was an
upstream  lead service  line.

  (iii) "Non-lead"  where  the service  line is determined  through  an evidence-based  record,
method,  or technique  not to be lead or galvanized  requiring  replacement.  Sampling  for lead
and copper  in the LCRR  in non-lead  systems  requires  additional  knowledge  of service  line

5. How  does  a water  system  document  each  service  line?

Pursuant  to the LCRR,  each service  line or portion  of the service  line where  ownership  is split,
must be categorized  separately.  Various  states  and the Association  of State  Drinking  Water
Administrators  (ASDWA)  have developed  templates  to input data for lead service  line
inventories.  Examples  from ASDWA,  Wisconsin,  Minnesota,  Michigan,  and Kansas  are
available  at the following  link: https://www.asdwa.orq/lead-and-copper-rule-lcr/.  In August
2022,  u.s. EPA released  an example  inventory  template  at https://www.epa.gov/ground-water-
and-drinkinq-water/revised-lead-and-copper-rule.

DDW has developed  a spreadsheet  that contains  the minimum  amount  of information  required
for a water  system  to comply  with the LCRR.  Water  systems  must make this information
available  upon  request  for each service.  Water  systems  may use the example  template
spreadsheets  above  to add additional  information.  Each water  system  must maintain  the
inventory  information  and be prepared  to provide  it to DDW during  sanitary  surveys  or audits  of
the LCRR  program.  DDW has created  a spreadsheet  for required  inventory  information  and
posted  the spreadsheet  on the LCRR  webpage  at
https://www.waterboards.ca.qov/drinkinq  water/certlic/drinkingwater/leadandcopperrule.html.

DDW will collect  the water  system-owned  and customer-owned  summary  inventory  information
in 2024.  A specific  address  or location  identifier  will be required  if any portion  of the service
line contains  lead, GRR, or lead goosenecks/fittings.  DDW will post the lead service  line
information  publicly.  Water  systems  are required  to notify  all customers  served  by lead service

6. What  information  does  a water  system  need  to use to develop  the required  inventory?

information  pertaining  to service  lines,  both water  system-owned  and customer-owned
portions.  u.s. EPA understands  that no inventory  method  is 100 percent  accurate,  but the
LCRR  requires  utilities  to update  their inventories  on a regular  basis as new inventory
information  becomes  available.  The LCRR  requires  the water  system  to utilize the following
information  to develop  an inventory.

*  All construction  and plumbing  codes,  permits,  and existing  records  or other documentation

  system.  (Example:  Determine  if there  is any ordinance  (City or County  Building
  Department)  that prohibits  lead lines, and its effective  date.)
*  All water  system  records,  including  distribution  system  maps and drawings,  historical
  records  on each service  connection,  meter  installation  records,  historical  capital
  improvement  or master  plans,  and standard  operating  procedures.  (Example:  System  tap

service  line.  The service  line can be visually  inspected  at the meter or valve box. If inspecting

service  line.  A record of the physical  visual verification  must be made by the water system.

lead paint test kits) to help identify the material  of the customer-owned  portion of the service
line. The water system should develop  a check list and instructions  for customers  and obtain a
written record and photograph  for verification.  The water system  will need to ensure the

Pipe diameter  can be used to determine  a pipe is non-lead.  Most lead pipes and lead
goosenecks  are 2 inches  in diameter  or less.  Some  3-inch  diameter  lead pipes have been
identified.  DDW will allow the water  system  to use a non-lead  designation  for any pipe 4
inches  in diameter  or greater.

NOTE:  When  physically  identifying  the material  of a service  line that has a split ownership
(i.e., water-system-owned  and customer-owned),  a water  system  may verify the following
locations or points: the connection at the main, the pipe from the main to the meter, the
connection at the meter, the pipe to the building inlet, and the connection at the building. A
water system needs to have a plan on how to verify the material of the pipe and connectors,  if
connectors exist, such as tails on meters, and determine if a second point of verification  is
needed for that portion of the service line. Not all service lines need to be inspected  at all
points. The water system must verify enough locations on the service line as needed to ensure
the inventory is accurate. The number of verifications will be determined on a case-by-case
basis by the water system. Verification of service line material on each side of the meter is
usually adequate to determine the pipe material.  The water-system-owned  portion of the
service line verification has been completed.  The water system may discuss their inventory
plans with the DDW district  office.

DDW encourages  the water  system  to classify  the actual  material  of the service  line
(i.e., plastic  or copper)  as often as possible  as an alternative  to classifying  it as "Non-lead."
Sampling  for lead and copper  in the LCRR  in non-lead  systems  requires  additional  knowledge
of service  line material.

Water  quality  samplinq  may be used by a water  system  to detect  the presence  or a lead
service  line.  Water  systems  may use the sampling  protocols  discussed  under Section  5.2 of
u.s. EPA's  inventory  guideline  to develop  a sampling  strategy.  A water  system  using water
quality  sampling  to identify  lead service  lines will need to establish  a community-specific

threshold  lead concentration  above  which  would  indicate  possible  presence  of a lead service
line.  The water  system  will also need to pilot the sampling  protocol  on a known  lead service
line and a known  non-lead  service  line prior to conducting  sampling  and identifying  unknown
material  service  lines.  The proposed  sampling  protocol  and pilot sampling  results  need to be
reviewed  and approved  by DDW.

Predictive  models  look for patterns  in a known  dataset  to develop  algorithms  to determine  what
material  may be at located  in an area with unknown  material  service  lines.  The predictive
models  are not 100 percent  accurate,  but they are a useful  tool to find areas that need more
attention  or additional  verification.  Any water  system  that finds  it necessary  to use a predictive
model  will need to develop  a plan and provide  it to DDW for review  and approval.  The water
system  will need to identify  as many service  lines as possible  using means  described  above
and in EPA Guidance  Section  6 and 7 before  using the model  to predict  the remaining
unknown  lines.  Using  representative  known  data on service  line material  will improve  the
accuracy  and reliability  of the model.  Most lead service  lines were  installed  prior to 1950.  More
accurate  identification  methods  will be needed  for older service  lines.

Interpolation  is a method  of using  known  service  lines in one area and assuming  other  service
lines in that area are the same  based  on date of installation,  contractor  used, or some  other
method.  Any interpolation  in a water  system  inventory  and the associated  data or
documentation  used will need to be approved  by DDW.

Interviews  with experienced  system  staff and plumbers  can be used to focus the inventory
effort and verify  utility practices.  Classifications  of service  line materials  based  on interviews,
however,  should  not be used as a sole source  of information  for the initial inventory.  Systems
may also consider  interviewing  their neighboring  water  systems  to inquire  about  regional
practices.  A significant  number  of field verification  is needed  to validate  staff interviews

Emerging  methods  of service  line material  identification  technology  are being developed  by
researchers.  Any emerging  method  of identification  will need to be piloted  by the water  system
on known  lead service  lines and non-lead  service  lines to determine  the effectiveness  of the
product  prior to engaging  with DDW for an approval  process.  All emerging  methods  will need
to be approved  by DDW at each water  system.

9. Non-Transient  Non-Community  Water  Systems  (NTNC)

NTNC  water  systems  traditionally  are connected  directly  to the source  and do not contain
service  lines.  Examples  are schools  and private  businesses.  The NTNC water  systems  will
need to inventory  all piping  from the source  to the building  inlet.  lJ.S. EPA is developing
additional  guidelines  for these  systems.

10. What  other  inventory  information  is needed  for schools  and child  care  centers?

The LCRR  requires  that each water  system  compile  a list of schools  and child care facilities
served  by the water  system  by October  16, 2024.  (40 CFR, §14"1.92,  subd.  (a).)

"Child  care facility"  means  a location  that houses  a licensed  provider  of child care,  day care, or
early  learning  services  to children,  as determined  by the State,  local, or tribal licensing  agency.
(40 CFR,  §141.2.)  In California,  licensed  Child Care Centers  are regulated  by the Department
of Social  Services.  California's  "Child  Care Center"  definition  does  not include  Family  Child
Care  Homes.

"School"  means  any building(s)  associated  with public,  private,  or charter  institutions  that
primarily  provides  teaching  and learning  for elementary  or secondary  students.  (40 CFR,
§141.2.)  A secondary  school  is considered  a middle  school  (usually  6 to 8 grade)  and high
school  (usually  9 to 12 grade).

11. Is funding  available  to develop  the inventory  and replace  lead service  lines?

Yes, the U.S.EPA  will provide  funding  to states  to help pay for utility service  line inventory
development  and replacement  of lead service  lines.  U.S.EPA  funding  will go to the State Water
Board.  The State Water  Board,  Division  of Financial  Assistance  (DFA)  administers  the
implementation  of the State Water  Board's  financial  assistance  programs,  including  loan and
grant funding.

13. If a water  system  is replacing  lead  pipe,  GRR or lead goosenecks,  connectors  or
fittings,  what  procedures  should  be followed  to prevent  lead exposure  to customers?

The LCRR  requires  the water  system  that has an approved  replacement  plan to follow
procedures  to prevent  lead exposure  to customer  during  construction.  DDW recommends  a
water  system  conducting  construction  on any lead pipe, GRR,  gooseneck,  connector  or fitting
to:

  *  Determine  the service  line material  on the landowner/customer  property.
  o  If the landowner/customer  is unwilling  to allow the water  system  to determine
  the service  line material,  the water  system  should  document  the interactions
  with the landowner/customer.
  o  If the landowner/customer-owned  service  line is also lead, the water  system
  needs  to inform  the customer  of the lead service  line and work with the
  landowner/customer  to remove  all lead materials  at the same time.
  o  The water  system  is not required  to bear the cost of the replacement  of the
  portion  of the affected  service  line not owned  by the water  system.
  o  If the landowner/customer-owned  service  line is lead and the
  landowner/customer  is unwilling  to replace  the service  line, the water  system
  may continue  the water-system-owned  user service  line replacement.
  *  Provide  the person  served  by the water  system  at the service  connection  with
  educational  information about the potential  for elevated  lead levels  in drinking  water
  as a result of the disturbance.
  *  Provide  the person  served  at the service  connection  with flushing  instructions  for the
  building  following  the replacement.
  *  Provide  a pitcher  filter certified  by an American  National  Standards  Institute  (ANSI)
  accredited  certifier  to reduce  lead,  instructions  to use the filter,  and six months  of
  filter replacement  cartridges  or an equivalent  certified  ANSI  point of use device
  registered  with DDW.
  *  Offer to the consumer  to take a follow-up  tap sample  after completion  of the service
  line replacement.

  1: Program  Goal
  What  does your  City  hope to gain from  this program/are  there  strategic  goals this program
  can help your  City  meet?  Through  this proposed  workforce  development  program,  the City of
  South Gate (City)  will  continue  its successful  partnership  with the Conservation  Corps of Long
  Beach (CCLB).  Currently,  the City and CCLB  offer youth crew-based  and internship
  opportunities  with the City's  Parks and Recreation  Department,  as well as with Public  Works.
  With additional  funding  through  California  Volunteers,  the City and CCLB  will  be able to
  continue  implementing  a successful  employment  program  for young  adults that focuses on
  projects  that address climate  change and resiliency,  food insecurity,  education,  and service to the
  community,  The employment  program  offers  employment  opportunities  to young adults through
  CCLB,  that also incorporates  hands-on  training  in park operations  and maintenance,  urban
  forestry,  orchard  horticulture,  and water conservation  projects.

  The overarching goal of our pmgram is to provide career training through youth
  employment and the development oflong-term career opportunities. All ofthis is done
  to help South Gate's residents address issuesrelating to climate change,food
  insecurity,  education,  arid public  service.

  The City of South Gate is not among the 13 largest cities by population,  making  the need for the
  proposed  services  that much more important.  According  to CalEnviroScreen  4.0, South Gate is
  in the 81st percentile  for its average pollution  burden.

  Section  2: Program  Design
  Which  focus areas will  youth  be working  on? Participating  young  adults will  focus on climate
  change and resiliency,  food insecurity,  education,  and service to the community,

  Climate  Change and Resiliency:  The City is in the process of green space expansion  through  the
  improvement  of existing  parks and the development  of new ones. Because of this, the City
  requires  a larger workforce  to help operate and maintain  the added park acreage. Employed
  youth will  participate  in litter abatement  and recycling,  trail maintenance,  urban forestry  such as
  planting  trees, installing  drought-tolerant  landscaping,  installing  drip irrigation,  and conducting
  general park maintenance

  Food Insecurity:  South Gate partners  with the Trust for Public  Land and CCLB  to further
  develop  its urban orchard  that promotes  urban agriculture  practices,  food waste reduction,  and
  healthy  eating. Participants  will  learn horticulture  best management  practices  to operate and
  maintain  an urban food hub, helping  to address the region's  food insecurity  issues.

  In terms of education  and service to the community,  young adults or as more commonly  referred
  to as Corpsmembers,  engage in ongoing  education  through  career pathway  skill  development  and
  skill certification.  For example,  this excerpt  from the Conservation  Corps of Long Beach's  career
  pathway  policy  provides  details  on career education  that takes place for eveiy  Corpsmember
  around urban forestry:

  Career  Training  Module:  Urban  Forestry
  Objective:  Corpsmembers  will  understand  the principles  of urban greening  and community
  stewardship.

  maintenance  with  VectorUSA.  Edge switching  provides  connectivity  for remote-site  end-users  to
  the core network,  city on-premises  applications,  and connectivity  to the Internet.

  a.  Authorizing  the issuance  of  a Purchase  Order  to VectorUSA  for  edge  data  network
  switches  for remote-sites,  licensing,  three years of maintenance  and the necessary  network

  Technology  Master  Plan (TMP)  prepared  by ClientFirst  Technology  Consulting  (ClientFirst).  One
  of the key  initiatives  of the TMP  was  an upgrade  of the City's  and Police  Department  edge

  installed  in 2006.  The edge data network  has reached  the end of its useful  life  and is no longer

  of one hundred  and its design  has evolved  to incorporate  additional  cybersecurity  components,
  including  network  segmentation,  port level  security,  network  analytics  and more.

  local  area network  (LAN)  switches  at City  Hall  and the  Police  Department.  At  that  time,

Executive  Summary

The City of South Gate is currently grappling with challenges posed by its outdated networkinfrastructure,
which has led to significant  operational  inefficiencies  and vulnerabilities  in network security, reliability,
and scalability.  To overcome  these issues, VectorUSA  proposes  a comprehensive  network  upgrade
tailored  specifically for the City of South Gate, featuring  advanced HPE Aruba technology.  VectorUSA is
providing the hardware, support, licensing and labor under CMAS Contract # 3-IS-70-0876AM  & 3-20-00-
0267G.

This strategic upgrade includes the deployment  of eleven HPE Aruba 6200 series switches and two 6100
series switches, designed to replace the city's legacy edge switching  systems. Additionally,  the upgrade
encompasses the establishment of a robust Point-to-Point  (PTP) link using two Aruba AP-677s, enhancing
wireless connectivity across critical city locations.

Key Components

  1.  Network Switches: Installation of eleven (11) HPE Aruba 6200 series and two (2) 6100 series
  switches, equipped with the necessary transceivers for enhanced upstream connectivity.

  2.  Wireless Connectivity:  Replacement of existing Wireless Access Points (WAPs) with a robust PTP
  link utilizing Aruba AP-677s, optimizing the connection  between the Senior Center and the Sports
  Park.

  3.  Centralized Management:  Implementation  of Aruba Central to provide a unified, cloud-based
  platform for managing the new edge switches and the PTP link, alongside the integration of
  approximately 11 existing Aruba switches from the Core Project.

Features  & Benefits

  *  Enhanced Network Performance: The latest Aruba switches ensure higher throughput  and
  reliability, significantly improving network performance and user experience.

  Seamless Integration: VectorUSA's professional services ensure a smooth transition  from the old
  systems to the new setup with minimal disruption.

  *  Scalability: The solution is designed to accommodate  future  network  expansion,  allowing
  additional sites to be integrated smoothly via change requests.

  Centralized Management:  Aruba Central offers a single pane of glass for network oversight,
  simplifying operations and enhancing security through centralized control and visibility.

  *  Cost-Efficiency: By reutilizing existing mounting infrastructures  and locations, the upgrade costs
  are minimized while still enhancing network capabilities.

  *  After-Hours Installation: To minimize operational disruptions,  all major cutover services  are
  scheduled outside of regular business hours, ensuring continuity  and reducing downtime.

VectorUSA's  network  upgrade  proposal  for the City of South Gate marks a crucial advancement  in
modernizing  the city's technological  infrastructure.  This upgrade transcends  a mere IT enhancement;  it
represents a strategic investment  in the city's operational  robustness, service delivery effectiveness,  and
sustainable technological  growth.  By implementing  this solution,  the City of South Gate sets itself as a

Phase  1: Project  Kickoff  Meeting
The project  will  commence  with  a kickoff  meeting,  marking  the official  start  of the HPE Aruba  6200 and
6100 series  switches  deployment  for the City of South  Gate. This meeting  will include  stakeholders  from
the  City  of South  Gate,  VectorUSA,  and  any  other  relevant  parties  involved  in the  project,  bringing
together  essential  personnel  such as the  project  manager,  network  engineers,  and security  specialists.
The primary  objectives  of this initial  gathering  are as follows:

  Introduction  and  Team  Alignment:  Formal  introductions  will  be  made  among  all  project
  participants  to establish  a cooperative  working  environment.  It's crucial  to ensure  that every team
  member,  from  technical  staff to project  oversight,  is acquainted  with  each other  and understands
  the roles and contributions  each will make towards  the project's  success.

  Definition  of Success  Criteria:  Collaboratively  defining  what  project  success  looks  like, focusing
  on both technical  and operational  perspectives.  Discussions  will center  on the deployment  of the
  Aruba  6200 and 6100 series switches,  including  configurations  specific  to the City of South  Gate's
  needs,  aligned  with  the city's  broader  operational  goals.

  *  Requirements  Gathering:  Conducting  a detailed  analysis  of the  City of South  Gate's  specific
  requirements  for the new  network  infrastructure.  This will  encompass  aspects  such as network
  architecture,  security  demands,  redundancy  mechanisms,  and  any  unique  operational
  considerations  crucial  for a successful  switch  deployment.

  Planning  for Detailed  Technical  Workshops:  Preparing  for subsequent  phases that  will focus  on
  technical  planning  and  detailed  design.  These  sessions  are  essential  to  ensure  that  the
  deployment  is thoroughly  planned,  covering  both overarching  architectural  designs  and detailed
  technical  configurations.

  Addressing  Queries  and Concerns:  Providing  an opportunity  for the City of South  Gate to pose
  questions  or express  concerns  regarding  the deployment  process,  the capabilities  of the Aruba
  switches,  or the  project  timeline.  This dialogue  is key to maintaining  transparency,  managing
  expectations,  and establishing  a trustful  relationship  between  all involved  parties.

Phase  2: Technology  Design,  Implementation  Planning,  Documentation  & Review
Upon  the  project  award,  VectorUSA  will  collaborate  with  the  City of South  Gate  IT staff  to review  the
network  design.  This includes  site inspections  at the City of South  Gate  Main  Distribution  Frame  (MDF)
and  eight  additional  Intermediate  Distribution  Frames  (IDFs),  encompassing  nine  sites  in total.  These
inspections  are aimed  at developing  an upgrade  plan to transition  from  legacy switches  to a new solution
managed  via Aruba  Central  and establishing  a new  Point-to-Point  (PTP) link between  the Senior  Center
and Sports  Park.

VectorUSA  will schedule  a stakeholder  meeting  to finalize  the cutover  plan and establish  a test plan based
on previously  agreed  validation  criteria  for post-implementation  testing  and network  handoff.  VectorUSA
will  conduct  virtual  lab testing  to verify  the  configuration  of all network  switches  and Wireless  Access
Points  (WAPs).  This testing  ensures  configurations  mimic  the existing  network's  SSIDs, IP addresses,  and
Layer  2 VLANs  accurately,  confirming  readiness  for deployment.  This phase  is structured  to ensure  all
network  components  are  prepared  and  tested  for  successful  integration  and  functionality  in the
subsequent  deployment  phases.

Phase  4: Network  Configuration  and  Installation
Upon  receipt  of the  hardware  by the City of South  Gate,  VectorUSA  will  stage  and asset tag the Aruba
equipment  in accordance  with  best-practice  standards,  utilizing  the storage  area provided  by the client.

each  new  switch  and Wireless  Access  Point  (WAP)  replacing  a corresponding  legacy  device  within  the
identified  Infrastructure  Distribution  Frames  (IDFs),  Cabinets,  or Outdoor  Spaces-designated  for  the
single  Point-to-Point  (PTP) link.  Installation  will  take  place  during  a predetermined  outage  window  to
ensure  minimal  disruption  across the nine (9) targeted  locations.

VectorUSA's  approach  to configuration  aligns  with  the network  design  that  was thoroughly  tested  and
validated  in a lab environment  during  Phase 3. The Switches  and WAPs, will be configured  based on these
tested  parameters.  GUI Templates,  as defined  and agreed  upon during  the Phase 2 stakeholder  meetings,
will be implemented  to standardize  and streamline  the configuration  process  across all network  devices.

Installation  also includes  the  use of existing  backbone  and patch  cabling,  as provided  by the  client,  to
connect  the  new  devices.  Transceivers,  agreed  upon  during  the  design  phase,  will  be installed  and
connected  to  both  downstream  and  upstream  network  components  using  the  client's  patch  matrix.
Following  the physical  setup,  the  project  will transition  into  a testing  and validation  phase to ensure  all
configurations  meet the predefined  functional  and technical  standards.

CALL  TO ORDER  Gil Hurtado,  Mayor  called a Regular City Council  Meeting  to order at 6:44 p.m.

6

PARKING  & TRAFFIC  The City  Council  considered:

  a.  Adopting  Resolution  to prohibit  overnight  parking  on portions  of
  Southern  Avenue  and Southern  Place adjacent  to South  Gate Park
  between  the hours  of 11:00  P.M.  and 7:00 A.M.  of the day
  following;  and

  b.  Approving  finding  that the Resolution  prohibiting  overnight
  parking  is exempt  from  CEQA.

  Arturo  Cervantez,  Director  of Public  Works,  spoke  on the issues of
  overnight  parking  and provided  possible  solutions.

  Fire Chief  provided  an overview  of the theft that was occurring  and how
  the fire station  would  benefit  from  removing  the overnight  parking.

  Carlos  Amador,  9293 Park Ave,  commended  Mr.  Houston  for his efforts
  in doing  what he can on this issue.

  Email:  Mario  Dominguez  stated that upon reviewing  the map, he feels this
  would  be a troubling  issue to prohibit  overnight  parking  as parking  is
  already  a problem.  He proposes  that Law  enforcement  should  increase
  patrolling  to lower  the theft  rates.
   REGULAR  CITY  COUNCIL  MEETING  MINUTES  OF MAY  28, 2024

6
PARKING  & TRAFFIC

CONT'D  Council  Member  Barron  asked a few questions  to clarify  which  vehicles
  are parking  along  those overnight  parking  areas.

  Council  Member  Avalos  asked if there were residential  homes  along  the
  marked  areas. She voiced  concerns  for residents  to be able to find parking.

  Council  Member  Rios asked if residents  are aware  of this resolution  and
  when  will  it take effect.

  Mr.  Cervantez  answered  with  explanations  of how residents  will  be
  notified  for a smooth  transition.

  Vice  Mayor  Davila  asked how many  residents  park in those areas. She
  feels it is a large area being  prohibited  of parking  and changing  the time
  frame  to better  accommodate  the community

  Council  Member  Avalos  asked what the protocol  would  be in notifying
  the residents  of this resolution  passing.

  Raul F. Salinas,  City  Attorney,  explained  that there would  be warning
  signs ahead of time  so residents  could  get an idea of what is happening

  Council  Member  Rios voiced  concern  about this area being  relocated  to
  other parts of the community.

  Darren  Arakawa,  Chief  of Police,  stated that if vehicles  will  be prohibited
  from  being  able to park overnight,  then they would  naturally  find parking
  somewhere  else. He confirmed  that once the notices  are posted  then cars
  will  be impounded,  and people  will  be displaced.

  Mr. Houston  proposed  pulling  this item and bringing  it back to further
  discussion.

  Council  Member  Avalos  made a motion  to bring  this item back and
  seconded  by Vice  Mayor  Davila.

  ROLL  CALL:  Council  Member  Avalos,  yes; Council  Member  Barron,
  yes; Council  Member  Rios, yes; Vice  Mayor  Davila,  yes; Mayor  Hurtado,
  recused.

1

  Ordinance  of the City  Council  of the City  of South Gate, California,
  granting  a ten-year  franchise  agreement  to Pacific  Pipeline  System,  LLC.,
  to use, maintain,  repair,  and replace  pipelines  beneath  specified  public
